bug_info.bug_desc: In boot/bypass mode, the main state machine did not pop the bypass FIFO while waiting in BootHTRunning. If a previous boot health-test phase failed, the rejected samples remained in the bypass packer. When a later boot health-test phase passed, BootPostHTChk popped that stale data, and entropy_src_core's final-FIFO push logic treated any bypass_stage_pop as a valid delivery as long as the transient ht_failed_q signal was deasserted. Since ht_failed_q only reflects the current/latched health-test failure status and does not tag the contents of the bypass FIFO, stale health-test-rejected data could be pushed into sfifo_esfinal and released as an entropy seed. The old push gating `(main_stage_pop || bypass_stage_pop) && !ht_failed_q` was not a safe delivery indication for the boot path.
bug_info.fix_hint: Modify entropy_src_main_sm so that BootHTRunning pops the bypass FIFO whenever bypass_stage_rdy_i is asserted, discarding any stale sample left from a prior failed boot health-test phase. When a boot sample is actually accepted in BootPostHTChk, assert a dedicated main-stage push signal. Then change entropy_src_core's sfifo_esfinal_push to use that dedicated push signal instead of deriving it from main_stage_pop/bypass_stage_pop qualified by !ht_failed_q, so discard pops never write the final entropy FIFO.
